questions.question: / a unit cost of Rs. 40 each. The following further data are available: Annual return on investment: 12% Rent, insurance and tax per unit per annum: Rs. 8 Cost of placing an order: Rs. 120 Determine: EOQ, Frequency of orders in terms of days
questions.solution_html:
• Economic Order Quantity (EOQ) and frequency of orders (Value Liberally)
  • Annual demand (A) = 60,000 units;
  • Ordering cost per order (O) = 120;
  • Unit price = 40;
  • Return on investment = 12%;
  • other carrying charges = 8 per unit per annum.
  • Annual carrying cost per unit (C) = 12% of 40 + 8 = 4.80 + 8 = 12.80.
  • EOQ = √(2AO/C).
  • EOQ = √[(2 × 60,000 × 120) ÷ 12.80] = √1,125,000 = 1,060.66 units, (1,061 units.)
  • Number of orders per year = 60,000 ÷ 1,060.66 = 56.57 orders.
  • Frequency in days (using a 365-day year) = 365 ÷ 56.57 = 6.45 days between orders.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Define Labour Turnover and explain its significance in cost accounting.
questions.solution_html:
• Labour turnover and its significance in cost accounting
  • Labour turnover is the rate at which employees leave an organisation and are replaced during a specified
  • period. It indicates the extent of labour movement in and out of the organisation.
  • Common measurement methods
  • • Separation method = (Number of separations during the period ÷ Average number of workers) × 100.
  • • Replacement method = (Number of replacements during the period ÷ Avg. number of workers) × 100.
  • • Flux method = × 100.
  • Average number of workers is commonly calculated as (Opening workers + Closing workers) ÷ 2, unless
  • monthly averages are available.
  • Significance: (1) high turnover increases recruitment, selection and training costs; (2) inexperienced
  • workers may cause lower output and more defects; (3) production schedules can be disrupted; (4)
  • overtime and replacement costs may rise; (5) it helps management assess labour stability, morale and
  • working conditions;
  • A moderate turnover due to normal retirement or movement may be unavoidable; the reasons should be
  • analysed rather than interpreting the percentage in isolation.
questions.final_answer: analysed rather than interpreting the percentage in isolation

questions.question: / period the departmental distribution summary has the following totals: Production DepartmentsService Departments P1 P2 P3 S1 S2 Total Overheads (Rs)800 700 500 234 300 The expenses of the service departments are charged out on a percentage basis as follows: A B C5 X Y S1 Deptt20%40%30%--- 10% S2 Deptt40%20%20%20%--- Prepare a statement showing the apportionment of two service departments expenses to production departments by Simultaneous Equation Method.
questions.solution_html:
• Apportionment of service department overheads by simultaneous equation method
  • Overhead cost as per primary Distribution Summary
  • P1 = 800, P2 = 700, P3 = 500, S1 = 234, S2 = 300.
  • The allocation percentages in the paper are interpreted as follows
  • P1 P2 P3 S1 S2
  • S1 20% 40% 30% 10%
  • S2 40% 20% 20% 20%
  • (1) Calculation of total overheads of Service departments
  • Let total cost of Service dept... S1 be X and total cost of S2 be Y
  • x = 234 + 20% of y = 234 + 0.20y
  • y = 300 + 10% of x = 300 + 0.10x
  • Substitute y into the first equation: X= 234 + 0.20(300 + 0.10x) = 234 + 60 + 0.02x.
  • Therefore 0.98x = 294, and X = 300. Then Y = 300 + 0.10(300) = 330.
  • Overheads of S1 dept. =X= 300
  • Overheads of S2 dept. =Y= 330
  • (2) Overheads Chargeable to Production departments
  • Over heads of S1 dept. = 300
  • Less overhead Chargeable to S2 Dept. = 30 (300*10/100)
  • =300-30=270
  • Over heads of S2 dept. = 330
  • Less overhead Chargeable to S2 Dept. = 66 (330*20/100)
  • = 330-66=264
  • (3) Statement showing secondary Distribution
  • Particulars Ratio P1 P2 P3
  • Overheads as per Primary
  • ------ 800 700 500
  • Distribution
  • Share from S1 (270) (2:4:3) 60 120 90
  • Share from S2 (264) (4:2:2) 132 66 66

questions.question: / completes the job in 9 hours. Calculate his earnings under Halsey Bonus Plan (50%), (b) Halsey-Weir Premium Plan, and (c) Rowan Plan. Compare the earnings under the three incentive plans.
questions.solution_html:

  • Standard time = 12 hours;
  • Actual time = 9 hours;
  • Wage rate = ₹80 per hour.
  • Time saved = 12 − 9 = 3 hours.
  • Time wages for actual time = 9 × ₹80 = ₹720.
  • Standard time wages = 12 × ₹80 = ₹960.
  • (a) Halsey Bonus Plan (50%)
  • Wages= (Time Taken * Rate) + 50%( Time Saved * Rate)
  • =(9*80)+50%(3*80)
  • Total earnings = 720+120 = ₹840.
  • (b) Halsey–Weir Premium Plan
  • The question does not state the premium percentage. The standard textbook convention of 33 1/3% is assumed
  • Wages= (Time Taken * Rate) + 33 1/3 %( Time Saved * Rate)
  • = (9*80) + 33 1/3 % (3*80)
  • Total earnings= 720+ (240*1/3) = ₹800
  • (c) Rowan Plan
  • Timetaken∗Rate∗TimeSaved
  • Wages = (Time Taken * Rate) +
  • (Standardtime)
  • 9∗80∗3
  • (9*80)+ = 720+180 = 900
  • (12)
  • Total earnings = ₹720 + ₹180 = ₹900.
  • Comparison Table
  • Plan Actual time wages (₹) Bonus (₹) Total earnings (₹)
  • Halsey (50%) 720 120 840
  • Halsey–Weir (33 1/3% assumed) 720 80 (72) 800 (792)
  • Rowan 720 180 900
  • Rowan gives the highest earnings here (₹900), followed by Halsey 50% (₹840), then Halsey–Weir at 30%
  • (₹800). The worker saves 3 hours under all three plans. Under Rowan, the bonus is linked to the proportion of
  • time saved relative to standard time; under Halsey and Halsey–Weir, it is a fixed percentage of the wages for time

  • * Halsey–Weir Premium Plan: The bonus rate ranges from 30% to 33⅓% of the wages for time saved.
  • Award full marks for correct calculations using either 30% or 33⅓%.
  • Wages= (Time Taken * Rate) + 30 %( Time Saved * Rate)
  • = (9*80) + 30%(3*80)
  • Total earnings= 720+72= ₹792

questions.question: / period the departmental distribution summary has the following totals: Production DepartmentsService Departments P1 P2 P3 S1 S2 Total Overheads (Rs)800 700 500 234 300 The expenses of the service departments are charged out on a percentage basis as follows: A B C5 X Y S1 Deptt20%40%30%--- 10% S2 Deptt40%20%20%20%--- Prepare a statement showing the apportionment of two service departments expenses to production departments by Simultaneous Equation Method.
questions.solution_html:
• Apportionment of service department overheads by simultaneous equation method
  • Overhead cost as per primary Distribution Summary
  • P1 = 800, P2 = 700, P3 = 500, S1 = 234, S2 = 300.
  • The allocation percentages in the paper are interpreted as follows
  • P1 P2 P3 S1 S2
  • S1 20% 40% 30% 10%
  • S2 40% 20% 20% 20%
  • (1) Calculation of total overheads of Service departments
  • Let total cost of Service dept... S1 be X and total cost of S2 be Y
  • x = 234 + 20% of y = 234 + 0.20y
  • y = 300 + 10% of x = 300 + 0.10x
  • Substitute y into the first equation: X= 234 + 0.20(300 + 0.10x) = 234 + 60 + 0.02x.
  • Therefore 0.98x = 294, and X = 300. Then Y = 300 + 0.10(300) = 330.
  • Overheads of S1 dept. =X= 300
  • Overheads of S2 dept. =Y= 330
  • (2) Overheads Chargeable to Production departments
  • Over heads of S1 dept. = 300
  • Less overhead Chargeable to S2 Dept. = 30 (300*10/100)
  • =300-30=270
  • Over heads of S2 dept. = 330
  • Less overhead Chargeable to S2 Dept. = 66 (330*20/100)
  • = 330-66=264
  • (3) Statement showing secondary Distribution
  • Particulars Ratio P1 P2 P3
  • Overheads as per Primary
  • ------ 800 700 500
  • Distribution
  • Share from S1 (270) (2:4:3) 60 120 90
  • Share from S2 (264) (4:2:2) 132 66 66

questions.solution_html:
• Wages under Halsey 50%, Halsey–Weir and Rowan incentive plans
  • Standard time = 12 hours;
  • Actual time = 9 hours;
  • Wage rate = ₹80 per hour.
  • Time saved = 12 − 9 = 3 hours.
  • Time wages for actual time = 9 × ₹80 = ₹720.
  • Standard time wages = 12 × ₹80 = ₹960.
  • (a) Halsey Bonus Plan (50%)
  • Wages= (Time Taken * Rate) + 50%( Time Saved * Rate)
  • =(9*80)+50%(3*80)
  • Total earnings = 720+120 = ₹840.
  • (b) Halsey–Weir Premium Plan
  • The question does not state the premium percentage. The standard textbook convention of 33 1/3% is assumed
  • Wages= (Time Taken * Rate) + 33 1/3 %( Time Saved * Rate)
  • = (9*80) + 33 1/3 % (3*80)
  • Total earnings= 720+ (240*1/3) = ₹800
